artists.biography:
Crippled Black Phoenix is a rock supergroup from the United Kingdom. Several musicians have contributed to Crippled Black Phoenix's albums and play with them during their live shows.

Members of the band used to play in other bands (including Iron Monkey, Gonga, Mogwai, Electric Wizard and others). In 2004, Justin Greaves began recording primitive sounds he had in mind for years. He was encouraged by Dominic Aitchison, and their ideas would lay the backbone for Crippled Black Phoenix.
Although originally having an unorthodox start, since all the band members were part of and busy with other projects at the time of the band's founding, Crippled Black Phoenix remained committed to staying together and forged their sound. The band writes what they call "endtime ballads," signifying both the slightly macabre nature of their songs and their unusual blend of styles as the final evolution in music. This blend has led to them being called everything from stoner-prog to freak-folk to doom.

Crippled Black Phoenix have made live shows a focus and have performed in unusual venues, using Victorian-era instruments in tandem with more modern instruments.

perplexity.description:
A Love of Shared Disasters is the debut studio album by Crippled Black Phoenix, released in 2006 on Invada Records. The project emerged from Justin Greaves' solo recordings begun in 2004, when the former Electric Wizard and Iron Monkey drummer started documenting musical ideas he had developed over several years. Recorded in Bristol during the summer of 2006, the album was produced through a collaboration of eclectic musicians brought together by Greaves' vision, with the project signed to Invada Records, the label run by Portishead's Geoff Barrow.

Musically, the album blends archaic and modern sensibilities through a hybrid approach that combines amplified instruments with Victorian-era equipment, creating a slow-burning, cinematic sound. The compositions function as what the band describes as "endtime ballads," drawing from literary history and contemporary narratives of loss and love. This sonic palette establishes the band's distinctive aesthetic—a dark, regal sound that emphasizes depth and gravity across its extended compositions.

As the first installment of a planned trilogy, A Love of Shared Disasters established the foundation for Crippled Black Phoenix's later work, though it was their fourth album, I, Vigilante (2010), that would eventually garner the band widespread critical acclaim. The debut remains a significant entry point into the band's catalog, demonstrating the ambitious scope and literary sensibility that would define their subsequent releases.
